findings.summary: Rig recorded win=true although the run ended on the LOSS overlay: any #screen-result.active counts as a win in the gate (trace t=75.0 resultText='TRY AGAIN', mazeDeaths=4, verdictNote='result overlay text did not clearly read as a win' yet gates.win=true), so the gated maze win is a false positive and the level's failure to reach the win path passed silently.

The ?ap=1 autopilot never reached the win path in 4/4 observed runs (rig run + 3 manual ?debugMaze=1 probe attempts): it lost all 4 in-level lives while eating only 61-78/136 facts, and death cells cluster in the wrap tunnel row (probe cells (2,13),(3,13),(11,13),(15,13),(20,13) with col 20 = wrap edge; rig stills show left-tunnel deaths at t=28.6 and t=73.4) because the bot's threat gate 'near' uses raw Manhattan distance without wrap so staff crossing the tunnel read as distant.

The level-title HUD line (setLevelHead writes id + title, ~70 chars) overruns the left HUD slot and renders colliding with the centered SCORE/FACTS counter ('STUDY HALL SCRAM…' overprinted by 'SCORE 00500 · F…'), illegible at booth distance.

FTUE controls hint is English-only ('← ↑ → ↓ / WASD steer · munch every fact · gold apples grant RECESS power') with no FR text, unlike the bilingual genres (nano-cure/rewind/world-tour/survival), and levels/<lid>/level.json carries no controls string at all for the booth's FR signage.

still-error.png was planted in evidence by the two known booth-logo 404s (assets/logo-all.svg and logo-in.svg referenced but missing): resource-load errors are excluded from the consoleClean gate but still trigger the rig's error-still capture, which a reviewer can mistake for an app error.
